title: Longitudinal biomarker progression and validation for predicting operational tolerance in a prospective multicenter liver transplantation immunosuppression withdrawal trial.
authors: Lopez-Diaz, Gloria; Sanchez-Lorencio, Maria Isabel; Inarrairaegui, Mercedes; Gonzalez-Dieguez, Maria Luisa; Cadahia, Valle; Otero-Ferreiro, Alejandra; Vazquez-Millan, Maria Angeles; Romero-Cristobal, Mario; Salcedo, Magdalena; Lorente-Perez, Sara; Sanchez-Antolin, Gloria; de la Pena, Jesus; Ramirez, Pablo; Pata, Maria P; Baroja-Mazo, Alberto; Herrero, Jose I; Pons, Jose Antonio
one_liner_zh: 该文研究肝移植免疫耐受的纵向生物标志物与机器学习预测，不涉及蛋白质-DNA互作或TF-DNA结合建模，与本课题无关。
abstract: Liver transplantation (LT) is a life-saving treatment for end-stage liver disease, but long-term immunosuppression (IS) is associated with significant side effects. Achieving operational tolerance (OT), where the graft is accepted without IS, remains a critical goal. Biomarkers play a pivotal role in understanding the complex mechanisms of OT, enabling personalized treatment strategies and improving patient outcomes. Additionally, machine learning techniques offer powerful tools for identifying predictive biomarkers and optimizing IS withdrawal protocols. This multicenter trial aimed to investigate the longitudinal evolution of genetic biomarkers during IS withdrawal and validate their predictive value for OT in LT recipients. A prospective, multicenter IS withdrawal trial was conducted with 91 LT patients. Tolerant (TOL) and non-tolerant (non-TOL) patients were compared, and longitudinal blood and liver samples were collected to analyze biomarkers. Generalized Additive Mixed Models (GAMMs) and logistic algorithms were employed to assess biomarker associations and predict OT. Of the 45 patients who completed the trial, 17 (37.8%) achieved OT. Molecular biomarker analysis revealed significant differences between TOL and non-TOL groups. Non-TOL patients exhibited higher baseline methylation of the FOXP3 regulatory T cell-specific demethylated region (TSDR) in whole blood. Longitudinal analysis showed distinct patterns in FOXP3, SENP6, miR31, and miR95 expression between groups. Notably, FOXP3 expression followed a U-shaped trajectory in TOL patients, decreasing during IS withdrawal and increasing post-withdrawal. Machine learning identified several key predictive biomarkers for OT. This study confirms the association between FOXP3 TSDR methylation and OT in LT patients and identifies FEM1C, miR31 and TFRC as promising predictive biomarkers. These findings highlight the potential for personalized IS withdrawal strategies, though further validation in larger cohorts is needed before clinical application.
abstract_zh: 肝移植（LT）是终末期肝病的救命治疗手段，但长期免疫抑制（IS）伴随显著副作用。实现操作性耐受（OT），即在无需IS的情况下移植物被接受，仍是关键目标。生物标志物在理解OT复杂机制中发挥核心作用，有助于制定个性化治疗策略并改善患者预后。此外，机器学习技术为识别预测性生物标志物和优化IS撤药方案提供了有力工具。本多中心试验旨在研究IS撤药期间遗传生物标志物的纵向演变，并验证其对LT受者OT的预测价值。开展了一项前瞻性、多中心IS撤药试验，纳入91名LT患者。比较耐受（TOL）与非耐受（non-TOL）患者，并收集纵向血液和肝脏样本以分析生物标志物。采用广义加性混合模型（GAMMs）和逻辑算法评估生物标志物关联并预测OT。在完成试验的45名患者中，17名（37.8%）实现OT。分子生物标志物分析显示TOL与non-TOL组间存在显著差异。non-TOL患者全血中FOXP3调节性T细胞特异性去甲基化区域（TSDR）的基线甲基化水平较高。纵向分析显示两组间FOXP3、SENP6、miR31和miR95表达模式存在差异。值得注意的是，TOL患者中FOXP3表达呈U形轨迹，在IS撤药期间下降，撤药后上升。机器学习识别出多个OT的关键预测性生物标志物。本研究证实了FOXP3 TSDR甲基化与LT患者OT的关联，并确定FEM1C、miR31和TFRC为有前景的预测性生物标志物。这些发现凸显了个性化IS撤药策略的潜力，但在临床应用前需在更大队列中进一步验证。
